sources.note: AETA Scoop5S-IP datasheet 12/2020 (opened, text read): 1U 19'' (WxHxD) 480 x 44 x 252 mm, 3.2 kg, AC 85-263 V, XLR sockets (2 female in, 2 male out analog; 1 female in, 1 male out AES/EBU), Ethernet 100/10BaseT. The S-IP is the IP-only variant of the same chassis.

AETA Scoop5 S user manual (opened, text read): section 3.2.2 all connections are on the rear panel (IEC mains socket, analog inputs female XLR, outputs male XLR, Ethernet RJ45); section 3.2.1 on/off key at the far left of the front panel, top left corner, hold 3 s (the unit has no mains rocker, it starts as soon as power is applied); section 6.5 says 1U 44 mm and 265 mm overall depth (inconsistent with its own 12.5 inch, so the 252 mm of the datasheet is used).

AETA rear photo (opened as image, 800x621, near straight-on). Calibrated 1.59 px/mm: plate height 70 px = 44 mm, giving a plate width of 444 mm (706 px); plate assumed centred in the 480 mm box (18 mm offset). The IEC inlet then measures 29 mm wide, consistent with a C14. in-send = ANALOG input A (female XLR, second of the left pair, label A); out-return = analog output A (male XLR, label A). Positions +/- 4 mm. ip = the RJ45 labelled Ethernet. power-in = IEC inlet at the right end.

AETA front photo (opened as image, 800x621, three-quarter view, so only a rough position). Opposite face = front. power = the round on/off key at the top-left of the front panel, about 10 mm diameter; read 15 mm from the faceplate left edge plus an assumed 17.5 mm rack ear, 30.6 mm from the bottom (+/- 6 mm). Protrusion d = 3 mm is an estimate.

Wave 5 re-measure of the XLR rows on rear_padded.png (the picture the ports sit on, 1.587 px/mm across and 1.477 px/mm up, read on an 8x grid): INPUT A female XLR centre y 18.7 mm (was 23.9, 5.2 mm above the connector), OUTPUT A male XLR y 20.0 (was 22.6); x unchanged (65.4 and 116.7 agree within 0.1 mm). +/- 0.5 mm.
